extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.publisher: Meta AI Research, Google Research, Carnegie Mellon University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process began with sentences from the FLoRes-101 dataset. For each sentence across 102 languages, three recordings were collected from different native speakers, aiming for a balanced sex ratio. These recordings were then evaluated by additional workers to ensure they matched the input sentences, and any invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Invalid recordings were discarded, which resulted in some sentences having no valid recordings. These missing sentences (about 21.5% of the dataset) were left as gaps to be filled in future versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source text data comes from the dev and devtest sets of the FLoRes-101 dataset, which consists of sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Speakers recorded audio for translated sentences, followed by a validation step where additional workers evaluated if the recording matched the input sentence.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Additional workers evaluated the recordings to ensure they corresponded to the input sentences, and invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Initially 3 recordings per sentence, resulting in 0 to 3 validated recordings per sentence in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers with a target sex ratio balance of at least 30/70%.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The first version of the dataset is missing about 21.5% of the sentences due to validation failures. Additionally, recordings vary in quality as they include both quiet and noisy environments without augmentation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to expand the accessibility of speech technology to a wider variety of languages, specifically catalyzing research for low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset collects the sex of the speakers to maintain a demographic ratio, as well as their status as native speakers of specific languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split into train, development (dev), and test sets. It is designed for downstream speech tasks such as Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Translation, Speech Language Identification, and Speech-to-Text Retrieval.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly hosted on TFDS and Huggingface. The creators have a maintenance plan to release future versions that will fill in the missing data gaps.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No data augmentation was applied to the audio. The dataset was split into train, development, and test sets with a 7:1:2 ratio and disjoint speakers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Recordings were manually evaluated and invalid ones were discarded. Text transcripts were tokenized, normalized using NFC and FST, lower-cased, stripped of punctuation, and split into characters with defined word boundaries.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: All recordings are kept as they-are, either from quiet or noisy environment, without any data augmentations ( e:g: SpecAugment [23], speed perturbation [24], simulated reverberation [25], etc.). We then split the collected data into train, development (dev) and test sets with disjoint speakers between train/dev and test, with a target ratio of 7:1:2.
